prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept, faithful reference-based visual development.
Recompose and extend the supplied historical Tequila Kill scene into ONE coherent active gameplay scene in the SAME original pixel-art style. This is a game screen concept, landscape 16:9.
Input roles: image 1 is the PRIMARY style/asset reference and scene to recompose; image 2 is the reference for map scale and overhead projection; image 3 is the EXACT reference for the character's in-game appearance; image 4 is the visual reference for the one objective bottle. Preserve the humble old handmade game appearance, the specific palette, texture language and overhead camera of these references. The goal is to show this old game in action, not replace its art direction with a polished generic western.
CAMERA IS ESSENTIAL: perfectly vertical 90 degree bird's-eye orthographic view looking straight down, exactly like image 1. Furniture shows its top surface. Players are small round sombreros seen from directly ABOVE, like image 3 and the three hat circles in image 1. Faces, torsos and legs must NOT be visible in gameplay. No three-quarter camera, no isometric perspective, no front-facing character illustrations. Horizontal and vertical walls and paving edges align with the screen.
ART IS ESSENTIAL: small 32px terrain tiles and 32–48px sprite footprints at an imagined 640x360 native game scale. Coarse authentic low resolution pixel art with visible stepped pixels, dithering, irregular hand-pixeled stone and sand textures, limited slightly muted colors, no antialiasing or modern illustration shading. Match the reference's lemon/pale straw yellow sand with fine diagonal grain, pale desaturated blue-gray rectangular cobblestones, ochre rocks and crates, dull olive straw hat tops, burgundy couch, muted brown wooden furniture, gray-olive long flat hard shadows cast toward bottom left. Shadows and outlines must be restrained like the reference, not thick black cartoon outlines.
COMPOSITION: A compact section of the sandy village arena, comfortably filling a 16:9 screen. Left upper area is a large open-roof rectangular stone-floored saloon, faithfully echoing image 1 with the same burgundy couch along the lower interior wall, three round barrels, a small rectangular table, separate chairs, and dark wall shadows. Large door openings connect this room with a broad sandy central courtyard. Across the courtyard, another smaller stone-floored room occupies the right edge. A few small ochre crate clusters, narrow worn wooden fences and low rock outcrops create clear traversal loops. Sparse small cactus tufts and gray rocks, matching image 1's scale. No skyline, no sky, no horizon, no visible building facades, no new monumental decorations.
ACTION: Exactly four small overhead players among the rooms and courtyard. Each player has the original round straw sombrero silhouette with a tiny gun peeking out, identifiable by a subtle red, blue, green or ochre band and a small matching ground marker. One small player crossing the middle carries the SINGLE green tequila bottle, a readable but small bright green object next to the hat with a small cream outline; do not add any other bottle anywhere, including furniture. One opponent aims a visible tiny gun and fires a single small yellow-white bullet toward this player; another is coming out of the room with two small dust puffs indicating dash; fourth is moving around a crate. Calm readable spacing, most pixels show the terrain, no oversized characters. Only short compact pixel effects.
No HUD, no portraits, no text, no title, no numbers, no logos, no watermark. No realistic gore. Do not introduce any visual influence from the earlier newly generated cartoon concepts. Stay strongly faithful to the actual supplied archive images. Keep the scale, materials and top-down sombrero language of image 1, improving only the composition and clarity needed for a living gameplay moment.
